title: K-flatness and scalar-extension projectivity for bounded ring complexes
statement: Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Regard modules as sheaves on their one-object bottom-topology sites [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $F$ be an additive functor from $A$-module sheaves to $B$-module sheaves with $F(M)=M\otimes_A B$ given by the shared sheafified change-of-rings construction [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $P$ be a cochain complex of these $A$-module sheaves, with integers $a,b$ such that $P^n$ is zero for $n<a$ or $n>b$, and suppose each evaluated $A$-module $P^n(*)$ is projective (linear maps from it lift through surjective linear maps). Then $P$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], and every evaluated term $F(P^n)(*)$ of termwise scalar extension is a projective $B$-module. No finite-generation hypothesis on the terms or flatness hypothesis on $\varphi$ is needed.

source.place: Lemma 064K (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism), bounded-above flat complexes; Lemma 0A6A (lemma-base-change-RHom), perfect-source computation, with algebra.tex Section 05CD projective modules

proof.text: For each term M = P.X n, every object V of the opposite one-object site equals the unique object. Transport hp n along that equality and apply Mathlib Module.Flat.of_projective to obtain Module.Flat A (M.val.obj V). TensorRight M.val preserves finite limits: evaluate each candidate limiting cone at V, use the Mathlib finite-limit preservation instance for tensorRight of a flat module, and apply PresheafOfModules.evaluationJointlyReflectsLimits.

Apply PresheafOfModules.isFlat_sheafification_obj to M.val and the identity ring map. The identity is locally injective and locally surjective by sectionwise injectivity and surjectivity. The module sheafification adjunction has an invertible counit at M, identifying sheafification of M.val with M. Map this isomorphism by curriedTensor.flip and transport exactFunctor across the resulting natural isomorphism. This proves SheafOfModules.IsFlat (P.X n) for every n.

Discard the lower bound in hb to obtain a bounded-above complex. Apply CochainComplex.isKFlat_of_boundedAbove_flat directly to the sheaf complex and the termwise flatness proved above. This avoids transporting total complexes and acyclicity through an evaluation equivalence.

For a fixed degree n, rewrite F.obj (P.X n) using hF. Construct N as changeOfRingsPresheaf applied to P.X n, equipped with Presheaf.isSheaf_bot; this is an actual construction, not an existential witness. The sheafification counit identifies changeOfRings with N. At the unique object N evaluates definitionally to B tensor_A P.X n, using the algebra structure phi.toAlgebra. Mathlib Module.Projective.tensorProduct gives projectivity over B from freeness of B over itself and hp n. Evaluate the counit isomorphism and apply Module.Projective.of_equiv' to transfer projectivity to the changeOfRings object. Termwise functor application is definitionally the term of the extended complex. Both conclusions are combined by And.intro.

lean.statement: theorem ringBoundedProjectiveExtension {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (F : SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose ⊥ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (onePointRingSheaf A)) ⥤ SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose ⊥ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (onePointRingSheaf B))) [F.Additive] (hF : ∀ M, F.obj M = SheafOfModules.changeOfRings (⟨(Functor.const _).map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)⟩ : onePointRingSheaf A ⟶ onePointRingSheaf B) M) (P : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose ⊥ (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj (onePointRingSheaf A))) ℤ) (hb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero (P.X n)) (hp : ∀ n : ℤ, Module.Projective A ((P.X n).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))) : P.IsKFlat ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, Module.Projective B ((((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P).X n).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)))
